exposure: labor phenotypes (no protraction, short protraction and vaginal birth, extended protraction with vaginal birth, extended protraction with cesarean birth)
outcome: uterine responsiveness to oxytocin augmentation (MVU to oxytocin dose ratios)
cohort: A cohort of 92 nulliparous individuals with obesity (BMI >= 30 kg/m2) and spontaneous labor onset.
finding: Labor and birth outcomes were found to be associated with measures of uterine responsiveness to oxytocin rather than MVU alone, with participants experiencing cesarean birth having the lowest uterine responsiveness to oxytocin.
mod_finding: Participants with cesarean birth exhibited the lowest uterine responsiveness to oxytocin, and the study suggests current labor arrest criteria may be too stringent for nulliparous individuals with obesity, as many can achieve vaginal birth with longer labor durations.
